comparisons.comparison: Both C and BAC report a decrease in their respective credit loss provisions or cost of credit for 2024, attributing the improvement to specific operational factors rather than broad market shifts. C attributes its $276 million cost of credit (down from $950 million) to a smaller allowance for credit losses build related to transfer risk outside the U.S. Similarly, BAC reports a $188 million decrease in provision for credit losses to $303 million, primarily driven by lower overdraft losses from fraud activity. While the magnitude and specific drivers differ (international transfer risk vs. domestic fraud), both disclosures highlight a positive credit quality trend driven by targeted non-economic or specific risk reductions.

sentences.text: Cost of credit decreased to $276 million from $950 million in the prior year, primarily driven by a smaller ACL build for transfer risk associated with exposures outside of the U.S., driven by safety and soundness considerations under U.S. banking law.
The provision for credit losses decreased $188 million to $303 million primarily driven by lower overdraft losses from fraud activity.
